groups.title: Big cats
groups.explanation: All four belong to the genus that can roar rather than purr.

groups.title: Snakes
groups.explanation: Each of these is a snake, and only the adder is native to Britain.

groups.title: Butterflies and moths
groups.explanation: Each name belongs to a butterfly or moth with markings worth the title.

sources.excerpt: The ancestor of the lion, leopard, and jaguar split from other big cats from 4.3–3.8 Ma.
The tiger and snow leopard diverged from the ancestral big cats approximately 3.9 Ma.
Despite being tetrapods from a cladistic prospective, snakes lack limbs completely, although pythons and boids retain a vestigial pelvic girdle.
The common adder, like most other vipers, is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young.
Cobra is the common name of various venomous snakes, most of which belong to the genus Naja.
The peacock butterfly is resident in much of its range, often wintering in buildings or trees.
One Pacific Grove site had no monarch butterflies in 2020.
Saturnia pavonia, the small emperor moth, is a moth of the family Saturniidae.
Vanessa atalanta, the red admiral or, previously, the red admirable, is a well-characterized, medium-sized butterfly with black wings, red bands, and white spots.
